### Step 3: Passwordless auth (magic link + OTP) (`identity-passwordless-auth`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).

Not shown: 0 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 2 code entry point(s), 2 doc(s).

### Step 4: Rate limiting (sliding window, fail-closed) (`anti-abuse-rate-limiting`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).

Not shown: 0 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 2 code entry point(s), 1 doc(s).

Not shown: 6 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 8 code entry point(s), 1 doc(s).

### Step 6: AI tool manifest & harness split (tool defs, risk metadata, registry) (`ai-tool-harness`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).

### Step 7: AI surfaces (chatbot vs deskbot split over one guard) (`ai-surfaces`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).
Risk: high — user-facing LLM behavior and permissions
Requires: ai-provider
Avoid when: The product needs only a read-only answer-bot — ship that one surface and add the acting agent later, together with its approval gate
Not shown: 3 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 8 code entry point(s), 3 doc(s).

### Step 8: Durable step execution (claim, lease, fence, receipts) (`durable-step-execution`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).
Risk: medium — leases without fences and app-clock leases are the classic failures; both are checked here
Requires: postgres
Avoid when: The work is one statement — a single transaction is already all-or-nothing
Not shown: 6 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 4 code entry point(s), 1 doc(s).

### Step 9: Deskbot approval gate (proposal → approve, plan-gated mutation) (`deskbot-approval-gate`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).
Risk: high — the safety boundary for AI mutation
Requires: postgres, ai-provider
Avoid when: Every tool is read-only or a reversible create — requiresApproval gates write and destructive risk only, so nothing would become a proposal
Not shown: 7 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 7 code entry point(s), 3 doc(s).

### Step 10: Untrusted-content boundary (the lethal trifecta, one rule per leg) (`ai-untrusted-content-boundary`)
Included as prerequisite (depends_on).
Risk: medium — the wrapper lowers but cannot remove the chance a model follows embedded text; the guarantee comes from leg 2 and leg 3 staying closed, which the gate holds
Requires: ai-provider, postgres (via deskbot-approval-gate)
Avoid when: The assistant only ever reads a corpus you own and has no tools that act or send — there is no untrusted leg to bound
Not shown: 4 invariant(s) that MUST hold, 4 code entry point(s), 1 doc(s).

### Step 11: MCP client (external tools projected into the one catalogue) (`ai-mcp-client`)
Satisfies: mcp authorization
Risk: high if wired without review — contained by default-write risk, fingerprint pins and the egress guard
Requires: third-party-api, ai-provider (via ai-tool-harness), postgres (via deskbot-approval-gate)
Avoid when: The tools are yours — add them to the catalogue instead
